The sculpture's name transforms it all into power: Quantum Universal Epic Era Now!

art.name: Radiolarian: A Walk Through Time and Space
art.description: Several monumental sculptures inspired by the microscopic skeletons of radiolarian plankton — ancient organisms whose geometric beauty underpins ocean life. Handcrafted from wrought iron, sheet metal, and fiberglass resin, each form transmits light: internal LEDs pulse, shimmer, and breathe after dark. A layered soundscape weaves together ancient oceanic ambiance, present-day marine recordings, and speculative sounds from distant worlds. The result is a fully immersive environment — a meditation on time, evolution, and the shared origins of life — inviting awe and curiosity about our place in the universe.

art.name: rage against the dying of the light // a field of swords
art.description: A field of swords with literary quotes meant to highlight perseverance.

art.name: ranawayhomenow
art.description: Burning Man can be both an escape and an arrival. This piece captures those contrasting feelings in a single message: a change in perspective shifts "ran away" into "home now."

art.name: Reactor Wing
art.description: The Reactor Project brings this futuristic pyramid altar. Play, hide, swing, react and interact with its beautiful geometry.

art.name: REAL LOVE
art.description: REAL LOVE is a multimedia project for Burning Man 2026 by acclaimed Ukrainian artist Alexander Milov. The project brings together a monumental sculpture — the final work in a series that began with Milov’s iconic LOVE, unveiled at Burning Man in 2015 — a traveling exhibition of miniature sculptures from the same body of work, and a participatory documentary film woven from visitors’ stories, exploring a timeless question: What is real love?

art.name: Reflection Connection
art.description: Reflection Connection is, in simple terms, a disco ball phone booth. It invites participants to both reflect and connect with themselves and others through its fragmented mirrors and light refractions. It evokes whimsy, turning the concept of a utilitarian phone booth on its head, to spark curiosity and wonder. It represents the light and sparkle in all of us.

art.name: Resilience
art.description: Resilience is a larger-than-life fire art sculpture of a Water Bear, otherwise known as a Tardigrade, our amazing microscopic cousin often hailed as the most resilient organism yet discovered. Resilience the sculpture calls us to contribute our energy and to ponder our interconnectedness as we strive for Radical Resilience as a community. This 10 foot tall interactive metallic fire shooting sculpture, simultaneously ugly, cute, and powerful, awaits our participatin to bring the Tardigrade to life.

art.name: Resonance
art.description: Resonance is a suspended pendant of forty layered panels whose shifting linework evokes ripples, tree rings, and waves of sound. Derived from the geometry of Black Rock City, the layered forms transform the city's familiar plan into a visible record of time as it approaches its 40th Burn. As participants move through the Man, the layers align and separate, revealing changing relationships between the vibrating patterns and framed views beyond. Looking back toward the city through the pendant's center, past and present briefly converge. Suspended beneath Cryptomeria, the work reflects the theme of Axis Mundi by connecting forty years of collective creation through the continual making and remaking of Black Rock City.

art.name: Resonance Tree
art.description:
The Resonance Tree is a large-scale immersive art installation made entirely of bamboo, designed by the Resonance Studio. It responds to sun, shadow, sound, and movement. Rising seven meters above the playa, the Tree invites people to enter through woven roots, climb through the trunk, rest in canopy nets, and gather beneath a living canopy of shadow and sound.

By day, its canopy filters the desert sun, and by night, the trunk glows from within. Hundreds of solar bamboo lights hung from the branches shift with the wind, casting shadows across the cracked playa.

art.name: Right Ear, Right Now
art.description: Right Ear Right Now invites burners to embark on a Q Tip guided spiritual quest, be vulnerable and open their inner worlds to the ear. The Q Tip channels participant's negative energies into the ear relieving them of their f-ears through the act of cleaning the ear.

art.name: Rinky Dink City
art.hometown: Penngrove, CA; Agua Dulce, CA; Los Angeles, CA; Davis, CA; Portland, OR
art.description:
Rinky Dink City is a collective celebration of the small-scale art of the playa. Arranged along a small city street, the artworks explore the essence of rinky-dinky-ness through scale, materials, and concept and empowers new artists to bring their visions to life. Rinky-dinks are characterized by approachable scale, creative use of materials, and focus on a vision over technical precision. Thus, Rinky Dink City explores the question: what is the essence of rinky-dink? What if art was fun? And can we all rinky-dink together?

Rinky Dink City is a celebration of community and collective effort, and will hopefully feel like everybody's birthday.

art.name: Rise (Float On)
art.description: A three-dimensional sculptural tower composed of weathered steel pillars of varying heights arranged in a stepped, organic formation. The central pillar rises 30 feet above the playa and features an attractively illuminated object visible only from the top, creating an irresistible draw upward.

art.name: Sacred Sun
art.description:
Have you ever had three days straight of rain (2025 maybe?) It's a bit blah. Have you had three days of straight sun? It's energizing beyond belief.

This piece is a show of gratitude for those that light up our lives whether it's the sun or other human beings.

The sun is also the center of our solar system and in keeping with the theme of 2026 (Axis Mundi) this will honor that. And at night our sun will still shine bright for all those that need it.

art.name: Sanctuary of the Silent Star
art.description: A mysterious celestial object. A 17-foot-tall lotus bud just about to bloom. Constructed from horizontally stacked, CNC-cut wood, its exterior is heavily charred from its journey through space. This scorched shell mirrors the protective layers people carry, while the inner sanctuary remains soft and tender. Inside, fourteen massive ribs rise to a central skylight. At night, LEDs push light through precise gaps in the wood, making the structure visually breathe. Serving as a monument to stillness in an overstimulated world, the space responds to its environment. When absolute silence is sustained, a glowing galaxy reveals itself. If the quiet breaks, the stars fade.

art.name: Sapta Dvāra (The 7th Gate)
art.description: Sapta Dvāra (The 7th Gate) explores the intersection of light, passage, and transformation. Inspired by the mythic act of walking through light to awaken inner truth, the installation symbolizes courage, renewal, and impermanence. A sequence of aligned gates forms a luminous corridor that shifts from quiet presence by day to radiant color by night. Motion-triggered light flows through the structure, creating a responsive environment animated by human presence.

art.name: Saturn's House
art.hometown: South Lake Tahoe, CA, United States
art.description:
Saturn's House pays homage to a core human rite of passage: the Saturn Return. This piece provides counter-lore to dialogues about Saturn Returns being gnarly and harsh — offering an uplifting, sacred, and creative reprieve that honors the 6, the cube, and the world-building energy of Saturn.

Cube is the shape of Earth, the shape of time, the shape of structure, the shape of Self. Cubes of Saturn reside in cities all over the world to pay respect to the God of Time. In Black Rock City — a city built in the likeness of a clock — this sculpture uplifts the architectural power of Saturn to create realities that support life, ingenuity, creativity, and power.

art.name: Sawubona
art.description:
Two chairs sit facing each other under the pin pricked starry sky of a Deep Playa night. Lanterns gently flicker on a warm red rug. A wheel sits between them begging to be spun. Spin it or don't. Sit and rest or don't. Speak or remain silent. Look into each others' eyes. Look at the stars. Look into your souls. Or don't. 

Find Sawubona and you might find something even deeper than you ever imagined.

art.name: Scared Sacred
art.description: Scared Sacred is a play on the balance between light and darkness. The lower half features a trunk that is entwined with serpent creatures and tentacles. The upper branches are adorned with backlit crystals and crystal chandeliers that emit a warm glow, creating a striking contrast with the darkness below. The intentional interplay between the trunk and the canopy emphasizes the balance between light and dark.

art.name: school
art.description: A  school of over 450 green transparent fish contructed of recycled 2 liter soda bottles swimming in three 15 foot repurposed trampoline hoops. Individual movements build a  constantly changing whole, illustrating the importance as us individually as we strengthen our  community.

art.name: Septima Stella Lux
art.hometown: Joshua Tree, CA and Sebastopol, CA
art.description:
Septima is a 28 foot diameter structural free standing sphere, comprised of the vertical intersection of four 7 pointed septogram or heptagram stars, constructed of large engineered timbers
A solid structural platform at nine feet above the playa will provide space to congregate and explore the structure from within.  
The perimeter face of each timber will be channeled for programmable LED's that will illuminate the sculpture at night. 

From the sacred to the profane the number 7 has woven itself into the DNA of our species, imbedded in our theology, spirituality, numerology & metaphysical realms:

7 days of creation  
7 Chakras
7 planets 
The number 7 is integral to Muslim and Jewish mysticism. 
7 pitches in the heptatonic scale 
the 7 deadly sins

art.name: Serendipity Machine
art.hometown: San Francisco Bay Area, CA, United States
art.description: The Serendipity Machine stands as a whimsical, steampunk-inspired installation, evoking the charm of an old-fashioned invention designed to transform the unexpected into positive outcomes. The structure stands as a gentle provocation for human connection, offering a moment of pause amid the chaos of the playa. Each interaction is designed to evoke reflection, emotional honesty, and spontaneous encounters between strangers. Blending analog charm with emotional depth, the piece transforms fleeting moments into meaningful ones, making space for surprise, story, and shared humanity.

art.name: Seven Sisters
art.description: For millennia, cultures around the world have told strikingly similar stories about a small group of stars in the night sky being seven sisters. Whether known as Pleaides, Subaru, Karatgurk, Dilγéhé, Makali'i, or countless other names, this constellation has held deep spiritual and mythological significance for peoples around the world, with some centering their calendar around its rising. The Seven Sisters is a three-dimensional model of this star cluster, allowing participants to see a familiar constellation from new perspectives and learn about the convergent myths told about it.

art.name: Shoe Tree
art.description: Shoe Tree is an interactive exploration of urban legend and rumor, inviting spontaneous and unsanctioned participation in deep reverence for guerrilla and folk art traditions. Salvaged materials and a roadside vibe let the passerby decide if Shoe Tree exists as a symbolic display or an unsightly eyesore.

art.name: Shots Fired Espresso Service - The Great Awakening
art.description: Our coffee shop is for the Builders of Burning Man. It is a highly modified Canned Ham trailer that is now has a tilt-out counter, a sound system, solar power, a fan, and a place for our team to keep their belongings.  The trailer is 16' long in total, so it only occupies a single parking space.  There are stools for seating, and shade provided by the trailer itself.

art.name: Shred Hard and Prosper
art.description: Take shelter and reflection as we evolve into the future. Shred hard and prosper.

art.name: Shroomie-Go-Round
art.description: This combines thrill and community within deep playa. The swinging structure has four seats, and can whirl you around in a circle. It's the perfect place to admire the stars and bask in the desert beauty.

art.name: SK8Z
art.description: SK8Z!  Once again Dragnet brings a group of artists' work to the deepest playa...40 skateboard decks will be placed on 40 T-stakes on the trash fence, each uniquely decorated and representing one of the themes and years of the 40th anniversary of Burning Man. Recycled, thrift stores, garage sales, found objects are used for  the subject matter...you may remember the tennis rackets, tikis or fish, just some of past art on the fence...this year will be the best, so please get out to the deepest point of the playa...BlinkingManCamp97 continues to bring it! A place where Excesssss just never seems to be enough...as we have said since our first year in the BlueLightDistrict: While the others are thinking, we'll be blinking.

art.name: Solar Prisms
art.description: Solar Prisms is a collection of cuboctahedrons comprised of solar panels and light diffusers. They capture light, store it as energy, and emit it again as a colorful and beautiful light show. They can be placed anywhere the sun shines and operate indefinitely.

art.name: Soul Tree
art.description: Soul Tree is an illuminated life size wire tree. It is a metaphor for life choices and free will, each strand being a thought or choice in ones life, the intertwined wires are self strengthening choices and actions, making branches that define a focus of our souls intention. Just as one can easily manipulate the direction of the Soul Trees wires and branches, one can manipulate their soul's trajectory through this life. No matter the past forces or decisions one has experienced, there is always room for redirection and restructuring. There is not one perfect Soul Tree but an infinite variety, everyone has the ability to keep growing and changing their trajectory. The only constant is change.

art.name: Spectral Scarab
art.description: By day, Spectral Scarab glimmers in the desert sun like a sacred artifact emerging from the Playa. At sunset, hidden light begins to awaken—warm ambers fading into deep violet as the sky descends into night. After dark, projection imagery blooms across its wings: celestial constellations, underworld tones, and radiant sunrise hues. Inspired by Khepri, the Egyptian scarab who carried the sun across the sky, the work echoes the Playa's daily ritual of dawn and dusk. Spectral Scarab becomes a modern Axis Mundi—a luminous threshold where light, shadow, memory, and rebirth converge. @tremendousmachinefarm

art.name: Sphere Vision
art.description: The two towering droids reflect the balance between creation and evolution, reminding us that as technology advances, it remains deeply connected to human intention and purpose. The LED Square serves as a portal to the universe, displaying celestial and fantastical imagery that inspires wonder, curiosity, and exploration.

art.name: Spin Your ASS!--Fun With Angular Momentum!
art.hometown: Ames, Iowa & New York, New York
art.description: Experience speed without distance through revolutionary angular momentum.  At the center of the merry-go-round, stand straight and tall and feel your shifting weight translate into revolutionary motion. Become the axis and have a look around!  Eyes on the horizon, and remember to BREATHE!

art.name: Spots
art.description:
Spots is a collection of oversized map pins appearing individually across Black Rock City, each eight feet tall, black and bold, outlined in reflective yellow tape. A six-foot flag pole rises above each pin, its label lit by solar lights at night. Every pin swivels so it can be read from any direction.

Each pin marks a specific kind of human moment: The Hugging Spot, The Giggling Spot, with more arriving in future years. They borrow the visual language of digital navigation and plant it in the most radically human place on earth, marking locations found on no map app.
Spots asks nothing. It simply identifies what is already possible anywhere two strangers stand near each other, unhurried, present, closer to something real than expected.

art.name: Stellar
art.description:
Stellar is an artwork representing nebula.
Through Stellar, we want to remind ourselves of the vastness of our world and how, on a scale this large, we, humanity, are a single unity rather than divided by differences.

(We don't want to minimize anyone or anything, but we do want to emphasize the wider connection we all share.)

art.name: Still Point, or "At the still point of the turning world."
art.description: Still Point traces the correspondence between macrocosm and microcosm, revealing patterns that recur throughout life and the value we ascribe them. The installation consists of two mixed-media panels, each approximately 12 by 8–10 feet, combining painting, collage, and gold leaf. One panel contains enlarged animal, bacterial, and plant cells, where cycles of birth, growth, movement, and dissolution unfold alongside fragments of human experience. The other presents an angelic figure juxtaposed against the solar system, her form divided into scenes of memory, value, and meaning-making. Together, the works contemplate scale and intimacy, transience and continuity, the reflective still point of conscious existence.

art.name: STOP and Reflect
art.description:
STOP and Reflect is a giant traffic signal in deep playa.  It is best viewed at night when it is brightly lit against the inky black darkness of the playa.  

Burning Man can be a frenzied experience...When the light is RED Burners are encouraged to STOP wherever they are, appreciate the art that surrounds them, take a moment to soak in the experience, form a lifetime memory, and move on again when green.

art.name: StreetLight
art.description: It's an ordinary streetlight.

art.name: String Me Along
art.hometown: The Oregon Coast, OR & Portland, OR
art.description: Packed into a small footprint, String Me Along has the ability to have a large impact. From a distance, colors and patterns stimulate their eyes. As they get closer, they see more of the color and even more detail in the pattern. As if begging them to play, they spin String Me Along using the crystal doorknobs and watch the interplay of color, patterns, and movement. Watching the large artwork spin draws more attention, inviting even more to play.

art.name: Sunny Side Up
art.hometown: Hong Kong, HKSAR and San Francisco, CA
art.description: sunny side up is an interactive and immersive architectural art and light installation that mirrors the horizon where the sun meets the sea, capturing the ephemeral beauty of sunrise and sunset. It reflects on impermanence and the quiet presence of hope, grounded in the natural rhythm that every sunset is followed by another sunrise.

art.name: Sunrise Sentinels
art.description: The sentinels stand in a line, waiting to greet the new day's sun. They keep our citizens safe, and warn all who would enter.

art.name: Surfwheel 2.0
art.description: A large surfboard pinwheel, made from hand painted, repurposed boards from the playas of Southern California, to the playa of BRC, inspiring awe as it spins with the wind.

art.name: Swan Lake
art.description: Dear comrade, come see the Swan Lake ballet on the playa, broadcast on all channels to your favorite television set. Do not worry why the ballet is being shown. Everything is all right.

art.name: Tandem
art.description: It looks like a tandem bicycle, weeeeeeee!

art.name: Tea Bag
art.description: Giant Tea Bag

art.name: Teeny Weeny Hooter Tooter
art.description: Teeny Weeny Hooter Tooter is a set of 4 small teeters that Burners can ride up and down on to create music.  The teeters operate leather bellows that supply air to 8 sets of handmade wooden organ pipes.  The walls supporting the pipes are adorned with additional random instruments and art to be played with and enjoyed.

art.name: Temple Braziers
art.description: The Temple Brazier is a wooden altar at the entrance to the Temple of the Moon, and serves as focal point for the ancient spiritual practice of burning incense (palo santo, sage, and others) allowing deep connection and spiritual expression.

art.name: Temple of the Moon
art.description:
The Temple of the Moon is inspired by the Queen of the Night flower, a fragrant desert cactus blossom (Epiphyllum oxypetalum) which blooms only once each year, at night, and whose flowers wilt before dawn. In this act of ephemeral beauty, we find a profound metaphor for our own brief beautiful lives on this planet, as well as for Burning Man itself, which blossoms each year in the dust of the playa, and then disappears without a trace.

We believe that this act of impermanence demands presence. The flower blooms for only a few hours. If you blink, you will miss it. The only possible response is to slow down, to be as present as possible, and to witness.

art.name: Tengri Oasis
art.description: Tengri Oasis is represented by a monumental reclining camel inspired by the nomadic cultures of Central Asia. Its three humps are formed by the exposed wooden frameworks of traditional yurts, transformed into transparent sculptural elements that reveal the geometry and craftsmanship of nomadic architecture. Three Altybaqan swings stand beside the camel, referencing a traditional space for gathering, storytelling, and celebration. Rooted in the values of freedom, hospitality, and connection to nature, the installation reimagines the ancient nomadic journey as an Axis Mundi—a symbolic link between earth and sky, movement and stillness, individual experience and collective belonging.

art.name: Tenseract
art.description: tensegrity + tesseract = tenseract

art.name: The Art of Becoming
art.description: Our hands are the spark of creativity.  They also connect us to others, our outside world, the infinite universe, and the cosmos.  We, as individuals, are connected to so much more around us, and as a collective we make up a greater whole and a greater community.  Our mini, magical dioramas will be able to be viewed via peepholes hidden amongst the tree roots of the Man Pavilion.

art.name: The Black Rock Guidestones
art.description:
The Black Rock Guidestones rise in defiance of the arsonists who destroyed the mysterious Georgia Guidestones - a formation meant to offer humanity guidance in the event of a global cataclysm.

A 1:1 scale adaptation of that intent, suited to our culture and moment, re-imagined in the desert. Three 20-foot, double-sided panels invite us to remember our responsibility to one another and the larger whole. Speaking across ages and languages, weaving from this shared bounty an earnest offering for tomorrow.

art.name: The Board Room
art.hometown: San Ramon, CA and Bend, Oregon
art.description:
The installation is a partially enclosed booth with two facing benches and a table at its center. It appears like a small room placed in the open desert, quiet, simple, and slightly strange. On the table sits an interactive art piece created for reflection, conversation, and play.
The piece explores the moment when strangers sit across from each other and become aware of the object between them, the person in front of them, and themselves. It creates a calm frame inside the movement of Black Rock City, offering a place where introspection becomes shared, social, and a little unexpected.

art.name: The Circle of Ancestors
art.description: This sculpture represents our common ancestors from the motherland, who watch over and unite us. There will be five ancestors, each 10 feet tall, standing in a circle of energy. The space is a place of protection and spirituality. It is meant to unify us and make us feel safe in communing with our ancestors. While standing inside the circle, people can pull ancestral knowledge and wisdom from the Earth.

art.name: The Conflux of Intent
art.description: A colorful large open stage area with a central covered pool with a deposit area is visible. There is a hanging face-type art sculpture on poles. There are shaded elemental-looking art seats and interactive elements surrounding the center area. The vibe is to rest and reflect.  The center area has a water feature for some sounds to be heard.

art.name: The Council of Animals, What to Do about the Humans
art.description:
The Council of Animals (What to do about the Humans) is a piece that explores our relationship with the other members of our animal family, and encourages us to think about what our relations might say to us, if they spoke in words we could understand.  

The goal of the piece, really, is to shift our perspectives, help us build a better word-castle to live in, that includes the rest of our family.  We have the power to change the future.  We've been in a rush for so long, as a sub-species, racing towards uncertain futures during troubled times.  

It's time to pause, stop, think about what we're doing, have realistic discussions about our choices, our plans, and our collective futures.  As one life, on one planet, with nowhere else to go.

art.name: The Divine Hand
art.description: The Divine Hand hovers above the playa, suspended between sky and dust. It is for seekers who understand they may not receive what they want, but instead what they need. Some pass without noticing. Others pause and feel something shift, through a quiet, personal gift.

art.name: The Division
art.description: In his poem, Mending the Wall, Robert Frost wrote the lines: "There where it is, we do not need the wall. He only says: 'Good fences make good neighbors.'"

art.name: The Eagle Of Entitlement
art.description:
This is The Eagle of Entitlement—a fully dynamic, entirely stationary shell of infinite reflection and fully realized, carefully rationalized deflection. The Eagle will beat all competitors' claims and will be the Eagle that you deserve, not necessarily the one you expect. 
It answers all of your questions with the proper replacements through a presentation of wonder and splendor, triumph and tragedy, based on historical trends and scientific data. Please remain silent and give compliance a chance. Understanding is a privilege, not a right. 

Regardless of age, sex, location, political affiliation, or musical taste, house music remains the only force capable of world peace. It is all in the message: a changing nightly journey through industry, art, civilization, invention, history, ritual, injury, spectacle, the laws of man—where applicable—and other wondrous and splendorful conveyances.

Its sound-reactive display reflects what it is given and deflects what it cannot responsibly acknowledge. House music is the only genre the Eagle recognizes as capable of inspiring world peace.

As not seen on HBO, the Eagle refuses to be tethered by anything other than the cables required to keep it steady on the playa. The other tethers are ours: the ones we resent, accept, inherit, attribute to others, and secretly wish others had. The Eagle rolls its eyes as it reserves and preserves your right to judge. "

art.name: The Flaming Carousel
art.description:
The essence of youth and nostalgia of past carousels draws people back to the fun and familiar.  Participants ride around on different types of creatures from the imaginations of different artists with rolling flames above the participants' heads, bringing joy to those who ride and those who watch.

The Flaming Carousel is a reworking of the classic carousel and revives the building of creatures with new materials from the imaginations of different artists from around the world.  It is both a sculpture and a platform for other artists to explore the medium.

art.name: The Garage
art.description: This is the Temple of the builders. A typical garage full of all the things you'd expect. Tools, storage, memories, seasonal things, equipment, etc. We hang out here and talk, drink, fix, build, jam out, play games, create and tinker. The Garage is the home of the laborers and builders who go unseen but make things happen. The hidden heroes.

art.name: The Golden Rule
art.description: A monumental illuminated sculpture spanning approximately 120 feet in length and 27 feet in height across the open playa. The installation spells the Hebrew phrase "ואהבת לרעך כמוך" — "Love your neighbor as yourself." Constructed from steel and elevated on slender supports, the letters appear to float above the desert horizon. By day the structure reflects sunlight with a shimmering golden presence; by night integrated lighting transforms the words into a radiant beacon, expressing a timeless principle of empathy, reciprocity, and shared humanity.

art.name: The Gothic Folly
art.description: A monumental open-air cathedral rises from the playa as a skeletal framework of towers, arches, and luminous panels. The structure evokes both a gothic ruin and a futuristic folly, blending sacred architecture with raw industrial materials. By day, sunlight passes through colorful translucent panels that resemble stained glass, casting shifting color across the desert floor. By night, integrated lighting transforms the framework into a radiant beacon of light and geometry visible across the playa. The installation represents a temporary cathedral for Black Rock City: a place where monumental architecture, light, and the desert landscape combine to create a shared space for collective presence and interactivity.

art.name: The Hitchin' Post
art.description:
The Hitchin' Post. 

Four un-assuming, Old West-style horse hitching posts have been placed around the Man for Burners to have a waypoint to meet up, hook up or engage in a Photo op. Their locations are intentional - to illustrate two playa aligned celestial moments with the Man, while also noting the seasons of the Axis Mundi Tree. Two Hitchin' Posts acknowledge the default world habit of human scheduling. It may even make you Curiouser and Curiouser - You'll figure it out. A couple of hints include "meet you at High Noon", or "lets hook up at Midnight". 

Go Hitch your Burn - Regards  CP + MM

art.name: The Last Shore
art.description:
The Last Shore is an interactive portal inspired by the disappearance of the Aral Sea, once the fourth-largest inland lake on Earth.
A freestanding frame filled with suspended reflective elements and transparent droplets creates the illusion of shimmering water suspended in space. As participants pass through the portal, a hidden soundscape evokes waves, wind, seabirds, and voices from the Aral Sea region.
Created by Stihia community from Muynak, a former fishing town on the Aral Sea, the work explores memory, loss, and transformation. It creates a symbolic connection between two former seabeds: the Aral Sea and Black Rock Desert, inviting reflection on what remains after landscapes change.

art.name: The Light of the Mother
art.description: The sun and the moon form a foundation for all life in our solar system. If you are patient you will be rewarded by harnessing the light of the morning and evening sun. If you linger, the moon's reflection will be in your hands and if you pay attention, it will remind us of the land we walk on.

art.name: The Love Nest
art.description: The Love Nest features a large wooden pelican carrying a nest on its back, filled with soft cushions. The installation is designed to inspire connection, community, reflection, and a sense of safety. As people gather within the nest to rest, breathe, and release, it becomes a living heartbeat of togetherness, a cradle for laughter, tears, silence, and song. Within this space, the nest offers a sanctuary for wanderers, dreamers, and the winged spirit within us all. The piece draws inspiration from a sacred space once shared amongst friends. In that place, they felt as though they sat inside a nest and were held, safe and free to speak their deepest truths. The experience left them bound together by love and wanting to share with others.

art.name: The Lust Stop
art.description:
The Lust Stop is the playa mutant bus stop. From its location in the deep playa, it offers BRC citizens an opportunity to board rides that might stop by and pick them up. We provide a route map of different bus/mutant vehicle services that might be in service with tentative schedules. As citizens wait for the ride, they can enjoy the comfort of a fur-covered bench and have shade over their heads as they enjoy bike-spotting in the deep playa day and night.

The lusty part kicks in at night where once getting closer to the bus stop Barry White and Co. tunes will greet you and make it a perfect sound track for a prolonged wait in a super comfy bus stop! Enjoy the wait!

art.name: The Man's Brain Project
art.description: The Man has had a Brain each year since 2018. It is made during the Man build using wood scraps from its ribs. It is designed to be placed in the Man's head, though instead, it travels the playa on a bike trailer to fill up with thoughts written on paper by participants. The Philosophical Center Potluck Noodle House and Lemonade Stand gazebo, on the playa, is its Home Base. The Brain burns with the Man each year. The big idea behind this project is to create an opportunity to make the Man touchable and Participatory. It is encouraged to share your thought with others around to give the moment an extra dose of psycho-magic.

art.name: The Market Commons
art.description: A circular arrangement of colorful plastic market stools rises from the open playa, inspired by the dense social seating found in Southeast Asian night markets and street food gatherings. The installation consists of 15–25 permanently secured stools arranged in concentric circles that naturally bring participants into close proximity. In a desert where seating is rare, the piece becomes both refuge and social infrastructure: a place where conversations, shared meals, performances, and spontaneous gatherings emerge throughout the day and night. Soft lighting transforms the structure into a warm beacon after dark, celebrating hospitality, human connection, and the communal spirit of public gathering spaces around the world.

art.name: The Only Way Out Is In
art.hometown: Dallas and Austin, TX; Joshua Tree, CA
art.description: A tunnel of 21 nested rainbow arches. Crystal prisms hang from each arch, scattering light across the playa. The passage allows participants to reflect on their past year, its storms and its rainbows. At night, the LED-lit arches glow across the open playa. It is a meditation on transition: a reminder that every storm passes, and that it is our strife that makes the rainbow possible.

art.name: The Oracle
art.description:
The Oracle explores the human need for answers and the vulnerability of asking questions out loud. Speaking to a towering mask in the desert echoes ancient rituals of surrender to something larger and wiser - or simply different from oneself.

The twist is that the "oracle" may offer wisdom, absurdity, or nothing at all. The sacred and the ridiculous coexist. A divine voice might offer life advice or ask if you've seen their bicycle.

When participants become the voice of the Oracle, the power dynamic reverses. They experience the strange authority of the unseen voice and must decide who they are in that moment: sage, trickster, or both.

The Oracle asks whether meaning comes from the answer itself - or from the act of asking, listening, and connecting.

art.name: The Orb-o-Chill
art.description:
Shelter × Intimacy × Recovery
This is a refuge for the weary Burner — a place of recovery after ecstasy. After hours of overload, light, sound, and the dense presence of other people, the desire to slow down, take shelter, feel the body, and return to inner silence arises. The Orb-o-Chill offers a state to experience: to lie down, breathe, be alone, or be beside someone. It is a soft pause within Burning Man.

art.name: The Paradox Post
art.description: Paradox Post is a kinetic signpost that playfully satirizes human confirmation bias. Built from scavenged materials and recycled community paint, the installation features four stacked, rotating wooden signs. Each side of the manually rotating signs displays perfectly contradictory advice, such as "Speak your truth" and "Silence is golden." The piece serves as a humorous oracle of convenient truth. Participants physically spin the signs until they align the exact combination of profound-sounding wisdom required to justify whatever decisions they already want to make.

art.name: The Point Being
art.hometown: Salt Lake City, UT, United States
art.description:
A cosmic spire emerges from the playa, encircled by a courtyard and benches, creating a space for reflection and group exchange. The intricately carved etchings on the obelisk's wooden panels depict celestial and earthly motifs.

By day, the obelisk is a striking silhouette against the desert backdrop, a reminder of our unique place within time and space. As night falls, the installation glows from within, symbolizing enlightenment.

Marked by geometric harmony, it encourages one to consider their journey, to recognize their unique contributions to our collective story. It is a place to ground the self within the wide expanse of existence.

art.name: The Portal of Collective Imagination
art.description: The Portal of Collective Imagination is a 20-foot circular arch constructed from recycled aluminum, bamboo, and mycelium-based panels. By day, it appears as a luminous geometric halo rising from the playa — open, inviting, and quietly monumental. By night, it becomes a responsive environment: light ripples across the structure, projections bloom within its interior, and subtle soundscapes shift with human presence.

art.name: The Race of Hearts
art.hometown: Deeth, NV and San Francisco, CA
art.description: Your heart is racing, your head is spinning. The Race of Hearts presents a physical interpretation of falling in love and the swirl of emotions it brings. Part steampunk automaton, part 1930s amusement ride, this heart-themed merry-go-round was conceived from Playa love and as a love letter to the Playa. BRC citizens ride the spinning sculpture on heart-shaped bicycle seats and arms engraved with emotion words. At its center, an armored heart opens to reveal two cartoon-style hearts dancing together. The armored shell symbolizes self-protection, while the dancing hearts represent acceptance, trust, and safety. On solar panels heart frames, BRC citizens write their Playa love names. The entire structure resembles an ace of hearts from above.

art.name: The Royal Trumpets
art.description: If art is how you decorate space, and music is how you decorate time, The Royal Trumpets do both. Dancing in SpaceTime, The Royal Trumpets create beautiful displays of sonic explosions-literally. 2 handmade pipe organ pipes on each of the six trumpets create the 12 notes of the chromatic scale. In the day you can find them making sound with compressed air, but come nightfall things get SPICY!

art.name: The Serpent
art.description: Rising from the playa, The Serpent forms a living Axis Mundi—a luminous bridge between earth, sky, and the unseen worlds between. At its core, a radiant spine of light pulses and breathes in response to the presence of participants, revealing that the energy of the city itself animates the work. Ascending toward the heavens while rooted in the dust, the Serpent embodies humanity's endless cycle of transformation—an eternal journey of becoming, where descent, ascent, and rebirth weave the story of our shared existence.

art.name: The Singularity Tree
art.description:
The Singularity Tree is a towering, cyber-organic solar punk structure pulsing with light and energy. Metallic branches stretch skyward, adorned with glowing LED vines that simulate flowing data. A central core emits a cascade of shimmering particles, creating a sense of movement and connection. Inspired by the moment where humanity and technology converge, the installation symbolizes the merging of natural and digital consciousness. As light flows through its form, it evokes a future where intelligence, emotion, and machine coalesce into one living system. 

The Tree marks the next chapter of human evolution. 

Axis Mundi.

art.name: The Solar Library Expansion
art.description: The Solar Library is a rhythmic repetition of triangular yellow huts with bright, sun-orange doors. The steel-framed huts present solar panels at an ideal angle to the sun. At night, they bathe in soft yellow light reminiscent of the sunlight collected all day. Artists apply for a library card so they can build battery-powered art, knowing they have dedicated solar charging capacity reserved to charge their batteries. The mission is to remove the noise and fumes of generators from playa art without the proliferation of panel farms.

art.name: The Sound of Time
art.description: The Sound of Time will be a large mechanical clocktower that will tell several different time scales, with gears of various sizes turning at various speeds. The moving mechanics will also be playing sounds, notes, bells, keys, gongs and more.

art.name: The Speed of the Earth 2026
art.description: The Speed of the Earth art installation enables participants to sense the speed of the Earth by carefully coordinating a mile-long row of strobes to flash at the rate of Earth's rotation at the latitude of Black Rock City. The timed flash rushes along the line of strobes placed exactly east-to-west, just as the Earth rotates, at the exact speed of the rotation. Standing still, a participant sees the flash moving in the far distance. In a second it is racing toward them. Then in another few seconds they feel the velocity as this cannonball of light zooms past them. It is a direct visceral feeling for what was formerly only an intellectual concept.

art.name: The Starting Line
art.description: The Starting Line presents a familiar race structure reimagined as a moment of beginning. It represents the shift from reflection to action, what is released during the burn and what is carried forward after it ends. Rooted in the idea of taking the first mile toward who one wants to become, the piece honors the spirit of a fellow Burner and the belief that meaningful change starts with a single step. The installation turns a recognizable form into a shared experience of intention, connection, and moving forward.

art.name: the weight of light
art.description:
"the weight of light" is a frozen moment of celestial reckoning transformed into an arc between the shadows of how we power our world and the brilliance of how we might transform it.
Emerging from the dust, a monumental lightning bolt commands the power of electricity. By day, the structure is a prismatic crystal. Its facets, crafted from upcycled dichroic panels, fracture light into a spectrum of iridescence. By night, participants can charge the bolt to create a massive, vertical lightning strike and boom of thunder.
Surrounding this central pillar are 8 lightning shards that form a 50-foot sacred circle. Each enshrines an interactive world that illuminates the "weight of light" -- the nature of fossil-fuel based electricity production, its environmental impact, and our power to transform it.

art.name: The Woman at the Core
art.description: These 6 panels illustrate the progression from nature through to cosmos using the motif of the woman as the core image.

art.name: This Blows
art.description: A decorated windsock, a returning playa landmark for every crusty burner to enjoy. It serves as a well-known wind speed and orientation indicator for all aviators around. Black Rock Citizens wishing to watch skydivers land can use the windsock to orient themselves for the best view.

art.name: Thoughts by the Edge
art.hometown: San Francisco Bay Area, CA, United States
art.description: A small collection of meanderings perched on a tree at the edge of the playa.

art.name: Time Drop
art.description: Time Drop gives you the ability to control the rate and direction of time in an infinite rain storm...and uses time travel to help people solve minor plumbing issues.

art.name: TITANIC
art.description:
TITANIC is a wooden ship, split in half, sinking into the playa. Dynamic, interactive lighting will illuminate the vessel at night, while flame effects will blast from the top two twin smoke stacks.

A climbable, amphitheater-forming sculpture for citizens of BRC to watch a performance or a sunset from, TITANIC represents the hubris of man and his faith in technology. As we continue to extract resources from the world at ever greater scale, will we find a sustainable equilibrium with the planet? Or will it end in tragedy? We are running the experiment live.

art.name: Totem of Transformation, The Shifting Balance
art.description: The installation presents a totemic stack of animals drawn from symbolic traditions across cultures. A tortoise supports a globe, with a deer, an owl, and butterflies rising above. Inspired by stories of the world carried on a turtle, the work reflects on humanity's relationship with the Earth. Each animal embodies a quality: the deer, gentleness, the owl, wisdom, and the butterfly, transformation. Constructed using reclaimed and repurposed materials, the piece reflects on consumption, sustainability, and the possibility of renewal, offering a quiet meditation on the balance between human activity and the living world.

art.name: Tower of Ascension
art.description:
The human ape, grounded and evolving from a single cell blob in a sea of primordial mud, pushes up towards the light, climbing the ladder of an elongated spine, reaching for the stars, beholds the glory and terror of its own existence, begins to comprehend its connection to everything, slowly realizing itself as nothing less than the entirety of existence, the eternal "I AM" looking through its own eyes, mumbling its own name, as its understanding expands into the entire cosmos. 
OM MANI PADME HUM

art.name: Trash Fence Souvenirs
art.description: Trash Fence Souvenirs is the only unofficial inauthentic vendor of the Black Rock Festival. TFS is a playful, satirical installation that offers inauthentic memorabilia. The offerings are intentionally humorous with a variety of tongue-in-cheek items such as: Burn Ur Own Man kit, Dust Keepers, Pony Parts, and Playa Trading Cards. Playa Trading Cards is our version of a fun educational way to highlight individuals, artists and artist groups, theme camps, mutant vehicles, etc. that contribute to the wonderful world of BRC.

art.name: Tree of Exhaustion
art.hometown: Black Rock City, NV, United States
art.description:
A curious piece resembling a tree, but not quite. 

A place for the exhausted and cosmically lost to warm-up and chill-out.

art.name: Tree of Photon
art.description: Tree of Photon aims to express the harmonious fusion of technology and nature, where photons symbolize the invisible energies that connect all life. It delves into the quantum poetry of light, where photons represent both scientific precision and metaphorical enlightenment. It seeks to bridge the gap between human touch and technological response, suggesting that, in an era of digital isolation, physical interaction can reignite communal bonds. Light-based art can evoke profound emotional responses, fostering a sense of unity in communal settings like Burning Man. It communicates that small actions, like a simple hug, can ripple outward, altering the world around us and highlighting our interconnectedness in an often chaotic universe.

art.name: Trinity:  Earth-Body-Stars
art.description: A 24-foot tall trinity of anthropomorphic figures, representing the connections of our bodies to the earth and our aspirational reach to the stars, have illuminated heads, and are designed to hold citizens' offerings of hopes and wishes. Imagery generated by AI, accompanied by music, will project hopeful future possibilities in how we will co-exist with AI.

art.name: Unhinged Lingering
art.description:
A freestanding architectural fragment: a standard exterior house door centered within two flat reclaimed-wood walls. The structure faces deep playa on one side and Black Rock City on the other, positioning the doorway between origin and possibility. The door opens to open playa, revealing not a house or destination but the horizon.  It explores limbo as a physical space — neither entry nor exit, but a moment suspended between worlds.
This installation is a tribute to the unhinged, the fine art of socially acceptable loitering. Freestanding excuse to linger with intent. A place to being everywhere and nowhere all at once. Lean in, take up space, and stay a while.

art.name: Unity Locus Focuser
art.description: The Unity Locus Focuser pulls in the universe's energies and focuses them into its spherical Third Eye. Participants walk along either of its catwalks to its Third Eye, then immerse their heads within it, experiencing the energy and views from within it together. Unity within the Third Eye is manifested through sounds, lighting, warmth, inspiring views, and the other participant's close proximity. The two sides of the installation are diversely different, similar to the opposing opinions of a polarizing issue, but that straddling between them is a unifying truth that helps to see things from a more holistic perspective.

art.name: Unpopular Music (or UNPOP)
art.description: UNPOP, or Unpopular Music, is an intimate listening environment in deepest playa. It features exquisite, detailed sound-works, including field recordings, abstract electroacoustic music, ambient textures, and other (mostly) non-beat-oriented sonic experiences, composed by many artists from around the world. Encompassing a circular space, the piece is built around eight custom-built Hemisphere loudspeakers, which enclose a listening area complete with comfortable seating.

art.name: untitled (omphalos)
art.description: Untitled (omphalos) is a sculptural installation composed of eleven burned firewood towers and two viewing platforms made from sanded, charred wood. Rising from the open playa, the work imagines the omphalos, the mythic center of the universe, as a place of threshold and convergence. The blackened towers form a gathering point between opposing forces: life and death, striving and surrender, doing and being. By day, the installation casts long shadows across the desert floor; by night, it glows from within and around its edges, creating a quiet field of light. Visitors may move among the towers, climb the platforms, touch the wood, and inhabit the charged space between endings and beginnings.

art.name: Up Nort' Art Shanty
art.hometown: Salt Lake City, UT, United States
art.description: Up Nort Art Shanty is a weathered ice fishing shack improbably perched on the desert lakebed where ancient Lake Lahontan once stretched for miles. Raised above the dust like a relic from another shoreline, it feels like a refuge for the weary burner wandering deep playa. Inside, a simulated ice fishing scene unfolds among fishing gear, odd memorabilia, and quietly unfolding stories of native cutthroat trout and prehistoric waters. Equal parts nostalgia, humor, and ecological storytelling, the shanty blends northern fishing culture with the deep history of the Great Basin.

art.name: VORTEX
art.description: VORTEX is a trio of illuminated cubes set against the open desert, scaled at 2m, 3m, and 4m. Each form is wrapped in a continuous black-and-white spiral printed onto tensioned Lycra, creating the illusion of a deep, collapsing void. By day, the stark geometry fractures perception against the horizon; by night, the cubes glow from within, transforming into luminous beacons. The work explores perception as unstable and subjective, compressing a sense of infinite depth into finite form and revealing how reality shifts through movement, light, and perspective.

art.name: Voxelite
art.description:
Voxelite transforms three-dimensional space into a canvas of light, responding to interaction with rippling patterns that seem to communicate in a visual language all its own. No two encounters are identical, as this photon playground dialogues with those who discover it—every visit revealing a different pattern within its luminous architecture. Venture into a realm where light doesn't just shine—it breathes, dances, and plays.

A metal tripod suspends over 20,000 LEDs in a hexagonal profile. Three complementing stations at ground level contain sensors and speakers, inviting approach with glowing bands of light.

art.name: Water in the Desert
art.description: Just as you found this water in the dust of Black Rock City, may you also find your own oasis in the deserts of default world.

art.name: We Hold These Truths: E Pluribus Playa
art.description: This mobile community recording activity moves through Black Rock City, showing up at camps, events, on the open playa, and by the ARTery. The title comes from one of the most recognizable lines in the Declaration of Independence, which marks its 250th anniversary in 2026. This project records short conversations about gathering, community, history, and shared futures in this unique moment and place. Grounded in exchange and collective reflection, it contributes to an evolving record documented by the Smithsonian, exploring the truths communities negotiate and share, while affirming citizenship as a practice of participation, responsibility, and care.

art.name: We The Sheeple
art.description: We The Sheeple reflects on the volatile state of the electorate; how rhetoric and weaponization of the media sways the masses as easily as the wind blows! Imagine an old world public square aesthetic: two wooden soap boxes equipped with megaphones face off from opposing ends of a field filled with 50 wind-driven sheep on swivels, all illuminated by Edison-style bulbs. Intellectually serious, yet physically whimsical. Very much red, white, and ewe!

art.name: Well, Well, Well
art.hometown: Eugene, OR; Seattle, WA;  Los Angeles, CA; Brooklyn, NY
art.description: Well, Well, Well is a full-scale wishing well standing in the deep playa. In a place with no water, it is the last thing anyone expects to find and the first thing everyone recognizes. A windlass frame straddles the rim, a rope hangs into the dark, and at the bottom sits a screen showing quietly moving water. When the crank is turned, a bucket descends and a short phrase surfaces, something between a fortune and a question. At night, light rises from the well, and sound drifts up from inside. The piece sits with the distance between what something promises and what it delivers, and trusts that language, offered in the right place, is its own kind of water.

art.name: What the Eyes Cannot See, the Soul Remembers
art.description:
What the Eyes Cannot See, the Soul Remembers

Two canvas installations at one of the entrances to the Man Pavilion at Burning Man 2026.

The work explores the idea of invisible songs, ancestral memory, and the connection between the seen and unseen worlds. It invites us to imagine what exists beyond what the eyes can perceive—memories, sounds, spirits, and ancestral knowledge that continue to live within us.

art.name: WiFi Jail
art.description: We are a group of children (6-13 year-olds) from China, and we have made a WiFi jail. We think people are imprisoned by their phones and screens all the time. Anywhere we go, people always ask, "What's the WiFi password?" We don't look up anymore. We wanted to show what it looks if we made a blown-up version of the prison we're carrying around in our pocket. As the new generation, we're growing up inside of this so it's even harder to escape. As a performance art piece, we will dress as little Black Rock Rangers, and when we catch people on their phones, we will put them in the cell. Phones - connecting you with people far away - disconnecting you from those closest to you. Unplug to reconnect.

art.name: wild free spirit
art.description: The Wild Free Art display is once again on the playa and will showcase original artworks. Created to share my vision of spreading love, kindness, and acceptance to everyone. Come and see what speaks to your soul and meet the artist. The universe is calling, come and see what it has to say to you through the art.

art.name: Windoors Vista
art.description: Tiny worlds are hidden behind doors within doors. Like accidentally clicking a pop-up ad, behind every door lies a carefully curated surprise, though thankfully none of them will ask you to update Adobe Flash Player.

art.name: windswept
art.description: Standing a commanding nine feet tall, this sculpture "windswept" makes the viewer look up. Made from industrial steel, the rigidity and durability mirrors the tempered strength of the feminine spirit. Her eyes are peacefully closed not in a sign of surrender, but of profound internal focus - the ability to find a centered "inner calm" while navigating external headwinds.

art.name: Wisdom Oasis
art.description: The philosophy of The Stump centers on the balance between nature and human creation. How life, even when altered, continues to flow through transformation. It reflects the cycle of decay and renewal: a fallen tree reborn through art, machinery, and water. The merging of living textures with gears and chains symbolizes harmony between organic and industrial worlds. The continuous sound of flowing water represents life's persistence, while mist and light evoke breath and rebirth. This piece invites reflection on our connection to the environment, reminding us that progress and nature are not opposites, but parts of the same evolving rhythm.

art.name: Words Left Unsaid
art.description: The project is an antique table and chairs with an antique phone made up in the past, with a Frame that welcomes you to words left unsaid, calls to the other side.

art.name: World's Highest Picnic Table
art.description:
The World's Highest Picnic Table explodes a familiar symbol of community into a monument. A table is the most fundamental thing humans create to bring people together. By scaling it sky-high, we turn this emblem of connection into a physical manifesto: the idea that community isn't passive, but something you have to actively build, climb, and claim together.

In the Deep Playa, it creates a surreal optical illusion. Because its traditional picnic table proportions are perfectly preserved, it warps your sense of scale until tiny silhouettes of burners at its top reveal its true height. At night, embedded lighting channels trace its structural lines, transforming it into a floating beacon of warmth, gathering in the darkness.

art.name: Yggdrasil
art.hometown: San Juan del Sur, Nicaragua & Roskilde, Denmark
art.description:
Yggdrasil rises from the dust as an echo of the ancient Tree of Life from Norse mythology — the living bridge between the spiritual and the physical worlds.

Reaching 22 ft into the desert sky and spreading 33 ft in diameter, its circular crown is woven with bamboo mandalas that breathe with wind, light, and human presence.

Built from laminated bamboo, Yggdrasil is both myth and experiment — a sustainable pilot exploring how bamboo lives on the playa and how it transforms in fire.

At its final moment, the tree returns to flame — completing the cycle between earth, spirit, and ash.

art.name: ZARVAN
art.description: ZARVAN, the ancient Persian deity of time, is a 23-foot interactive sculpture in the form of a monumental human head that explores perception, communication, and collective presence. Visitors can look through internal periscopes aligned with the eyes to experience the surrounding landscape through ZARVAN’s gaze. Integrated speaking tubes within the ears allow people on opposite sides of the sculpture to speak and listen through the structure itself, making the work a vessel for human connection and shared presence. Its luminous crown, inspired by traditional Persian stained glass, responds to human presence with shifting colored light, while the faceted steel body draws from Persian rug geometry and is hand painted with Persian rug motifs, embedding cultural memory into the form. Through sight, sound, and participation, ZARVAN becomes a living, responsive system.

mutant_vehicles.name: ¡AXOLOLT! The Earth Guardian
mutant_vehicles.description:
¡AXOLOTL! is a monumental (16 meter / (50') art vehicle and concert soundstage which provides an inspirational and collaborative platform for tours, live performances and events at Black Rock City and beyond.

Taking its name and inspiration from an endangered amphibian endemic to the wetlands of Mexico City, Axololt are revolutionizing human medical science through its capacity to regenerate, Ultimately, ¡AXOLOTL! is both a platform for creative expression and a powerful symbol of life's endurance.

mutant_vehicles.name: A Streetcar Named DESIRE
mutant_vehicles.description:
A Streetcar Named Desire. Transport vehicle with authentic Streetcar roof system. Design includes handicap access
and wheelchair access (2). Can accommodate 16(+)(-) comfortably.

mutant_vehicles.name: Abraxas
mutant_vehicles.description:
Abraxas Dragon has been on playa since 2006, providing incredible music, art and vibes. 

Abraxas is partnered with the Non-Profit Grassroots Aid Partnership and assists with Disaster Relief, notably for Hurricane Helene in North Carolina as well as Moonlight Orphanage in Uganda, Africa. 

Abraxas has participated in ground-breaking events such as: Catharsis on the Mall in D.C., and M.A.P.S Psychedelic Conference in Denver.

Abraxas has a history of being one of the most recognizable and photogenic art cars on the playa.

mutant_vehicles.name: Abu the Horsefly
mutant_vehicles.description: Abu is inspired by the 1986 animated movie by Studio Miyazaki "Nausicaa of the Valley of the Wind." This is the first insect that Princess Nausicaa defends from the angry mob. She helps Abu to find its way home. Abu teaches us that fear and mistrust are the real evils in this world, and only together we can make a difference.

mutant_vehicles.name: Airpusher, The Solarpunk Airship
mutant_vehicles.description:
Once upon a time, a group of silly dreamers decided it was time to create another art car for the Burning Man Community. The idea was based on if DJ's want a platform to DJ, then they need to build and support their own platform! From our humble start, this family is now 40 core strong. We are working hard to bring the best in art and music to the burner community and beyond. Airpusher, in its current form, is over a decade old this year! Happy 12th
Birthday, Airpusher!

mutant_vehicles.name: Aldo
mutant_vehicles.description: Aldo is a suave mustachio of a guy that rolls jolly.

mutant_vehicles.name: Alladin's Lamp: Making Playa Dreams Come True
mutant_vehicles.description: Alladin's Lamp is a work of mobile art recreating the "bottom of the genie bottle" experience for those in need of comfort in the midst of the desert. Riders are surrounded by colorful cushions and blankets, excellently curated music, and an opportunity to ride the Playa with their fellow burners.

mutant_vehicles.name: Animal car
mutant_vehicles.description: Animal Car.

mutant_vehicles.name: AntiDysentery
mutant_vehicles.description: The AntiDysentery Conestoga wagon is capable of discharging flames at over 1.5 million BTU's.

mutant_vehicles.name: Anubis
mutant_vehicles.description: Anubis is a majestic Egyptian palanquin, borne aloft by four articulated statues of the god Anubis. Atop the lavishly adorned platform, the Pharaoh and their passengers embark on a journey through the veil of the afterlife. Intricately detailed with tapestries, flowing drapery, and exquisite cast and carved artworks, the vehicle radiates an otherworldly presence, illuminated by vibrant colored lights.

mutant_vehicles.name: Apollonia
mutant_vehicles.description: Apollonia is an EV Mutant Vehicle that is made of 61 LED rings and edge light dichroic acrylic. The tangent circles carapace reflects the light of the playa in beautiful colors during the day, and at night are a delight of LED's animations. Apollonia is pure geometry and color without a literal reference, triggering the imagination about its possible origins and inspiration.

mutant_vehicles.name: AquaZone Mobile Hydration Station
mutant_vehicles.description: a beacon of hydration... A blue wave rising high in the midst of one of the driest places on earth, promising to slake your thirst and provide respite... a true oasis on wheels.

mutant_vehicles.name: Arabella
mutant_vehicles.description:
Arabella is a beautiful Art Nouveau phoenix with stunning lighting and dramatic flame effects as well as a luxurious bar and lounge area inside. 

Arabella rises from the ashes of our last art car, the Dodo, which has gone the way of the dodo. As was the case with our lamented Dodo, we seek to make Arabella a traveling party, and to adapt the atmosphere to the situation. We hope that the bar will see philosophical debates, impromptu dance parties, and the beginning of more than a few lasting friendships. As such, we expect that you will often find languid burners relaxing in the bar area with delicious specialty cocktails. We also hope to have numerous performances on the roof deck from both DJs and live bands in the years to come.

mutant_vehicles.name: Astral Plain
mutant_vehicles.description: Astral Plain is a warmly lit mutant vehicle designed as a mobile conversation lounge, offering a peaceful and inviting space for introspection, connection, and meaningful dialogue through esoteric experiences.

mutant_vehicles.name: Automan
mutant_vehicles.description: The Automan is the world's largest automated ottoman!

mutant_vehicles.name: Axolitl
mutant_vehicles.description: Axolotl's Little Buddy -- Axolitl

mutant_vehicles.name: Azeban - The Trash Panda
mutant_vehicles.description: Azeban the Trash Panda is a raccoon art car, lighting up the night and seeking out the people, places and mischief which make Burning Man so unique.

mutant_vehicles.name: BAAAHS
mutant_vehicles.description: BAAAHS is the Big Ass Awesomely Amazing Homosexual Sheep. He has laser eyes and killer parties, and boy does she ever sparkle at night. BAAAHS is radically queer, flamboyantly friendly to all, and a pulsing beacon for weirdness on the playa. BAAAHS wants you inside.

mutant_vehicles.name: baby buggy
mutant_vehicles.description: 50s style baby buggy

mutant_vehicles.name: Baby Shark Fin
mutant_vehicles.description: The shark ate too many metal cans and swims under the playa. Watch out and get a bigger boat!

mutant_vehicles.name: Badillac
mutant_vehicles.description:
"Badillac" by J.C. Adams is a striking art car that seamlessly blends the opulence of a 1969 Cadillac DeVille with a bold, post-apocalyptic edge. This unique creation fuses classic Americana with radical design, reimagining a world where timeless elegance meets survival.
Crafted with meticulous attention to detail, "Badillac" boasts a handcrafted body of steel, exotic woods, fiberglass, and supple leather, embodying a refined yet resilient aesthetic. Its exterior evokes a journey through time, from the rugged landscapes of the Wild West to a futuristic vision where grit and glamour coexist.

mutant_vehicles.name: Barbie Whorehouse
mutant_vehicles.description: It is a spicy version of the well known Barbie Play House with hot pink exterior and purple accents. Riders enjoy the comfort of the first level or the second level balcony.

mutant_vehicles.name: Bass Snail
mutant_vehicles.description: The Bass Snail transforms a classic chassis into a glowing, prehistoric wonder. With a custom wood frame, a massive PVC shell, and a sculptural mushroom roof, this creature serves as a beacon of wonder in the deep playa night. Beyond aesthetics, the Bass Snail is a gift of mobility. Rooted in Radical Inclusion, we prioritize gifting rides to those with ADA needs. We invite you to climb aboard our low-entry foot, find a seat under the mushroom, and enjoy a magical, inclusive journey home.

mutant_vehicles.name: Bay Squatch
mutant_vehicles.description: Bay Squatch It is a wave runner jet ski with an 80s neon Sasquatch, meets Miami power ballad beach party.

mutant_vehicles.name: Beautiful Engine
mutant_vehicles.description: Beautiful Engine is a small Moroccan style palanquin-like mutant vehicle, designed to transport burners in a comfy, fuzzy bed. Originally part of a fleet, has gained its own unique character with some extra mutations by the new owners (since 2017).

mutant_vehicles.name: BeOnTv
mutant_vehicles.description:
BeOnTv is a a mobile television and a public performance stage art car where the rider is in the TV and "OnTV" - an integral part of the ride and the entertainment.
Riders will be able to enact "programmed" television shows, dance, or exercise their extroverted mojo.

mutant_vehicles.name: Big Bubby
mutant_vehicles.description: A custom designed and built, convertible, roaming, bike shop

mutant_vehicles.name: Big Bunny
mutant_vehicles.description: The Big Bunny is pink, furry, welcoming, loving…good vibes only! Dj driven playing funky dirty house music we have a great sound system to get down to. GET ON THE BUNNY ❤️

mutant_vehicles.name: BigKrabCar
mutant_vehicles.description: For the 4nd year on Playa we present BigKrabCar, a Krusty and Dusty Krab for your sideways riding adventures, in, around and all the way to the trash fence of Black Rock City 2026!

mutant_vehicles.name: BiPolar Express 1
mutant_vehicles.description: BiPolar Express is a train that will carry you away into a surreal music journey. Two locomotives facing polar directions bring a large sound system setup as well as the mesmerising laser and light experience for burners on the Playa. It provides a central space where participants can come together, connect with one another, and share experiences while enjoying live performances and DJ sets.

mutant_vehicles.name: BiPolar Express 2
mutant_vehicles.description: BiPolar Express is a train that will carry you away into a futuristic music journey. Two locomotives facing polar directions bring a large sound system setup as well as the mesmerising laser and light experience for burners on the Playa. It provides a central space where participants can come together, connect with one another, and share experiences while enjoying live performances and DJ sets.

mutant_vehicles.name: BLACK ROCK BANDIT
mutant_vehicles.description: Larger-than-life interactive slot machine with revolving reels, jackpots and pay-outs.

mutant_vehicles.name: Black Rock Bomber
mutant_vehicles.description: Silver cart sized Black Rock Bomber

mutant_vehicles.name: BLACK ROCK CIRCUS WAGON
mutant_vehicles.description: A trained gorilla on a giant unicycle pulls the Black Rock Circus Wagon across the playa!

mutant_vehicles.name: Black Rock City Interplanetary Towing Co.
mutant_vehicles.description: Turning Planets in Portals for your towing pleasure! Safety Third!

mutant_vehicles.name: Blazing Death Ship
mutant_vehicles.description: The Death Ship is a Viking funeral boat that was ripped from the seas of the 10th century and hurtled through dimensional rifts, where she completed the three trials. She has now returned to earth, transformed into a sentient murder boat.  She's devoured many enemies! Traveled to another dimension! Ran for local municipal councils!  She is 30 feet long, 20 feet tall, and benches something like 415 lbs. She's defeated many in single combat. Zero lasers.

mutant_vehicles.name: Blue Bull
mutant_vehicles.description:
"Blue Bull" is a mutant vehicle inspired by Maria Prymachenko's 1947 artwork of the same name, transforming Ukrainian folk art into a bold, mobile presence on the playa.
Covered in plush, UV-reactive blue fur, this monumental creature glows at night and moves through Black Rock City with immersive sound and dynamic lighting. Sunset and select evening DJ sets activate it as a vibrant yet welcoming gathering space.
More than a sound vehicle, Blue Bull is a roaming cultural statement — a living interpretation of Ukrainian artistic heritage, reimagined as a surreal, participatory environment where people meet, dance, and share in a collective moment of creativity.

mutant_vehicles.name: Bone Voyage
mutant_vehicles.description: Extinction couldn't stop us! Prehistoric oasis roaming the dust. Part mammoth, part tropical sanctuary, we invite you to step inside our lounge or ascend to the belly of the beast for chilled drinks and desert views. A nomadic relic connecting the ancient past to the spirit of the playa.

mutant_vehicles.name: Boogie Bug
mutant_vehicles.description: Boogie Bug Inflatable Mutant Vehicle - Come take a ride with us and enjoy the music and fun.

mutant_vehicles.name: Boy Lady Bug
mutant_vehicles.description: Come take a ride across the playa in The Boy Lady Bug!

mutant_vehicles.name: BrainCar
mutant_vehicles.description: Is it a cloud... or a brain? Perhaps a rabbit with its ears up? You decide! Spot the curious little internal organ trundling through the dust or lighting up the night.

mutant_vehicles.name: Bubblegasm
mutant_vehicles.description: Bubblegasm was  built to spread joy with all who ride on her or dance and play around her. Bubbles are a metaphor for life, fleeting and fragile and are a reminder about how precious our time is while we are here, and to make the most of each moment. And like each bubble, each person and their life is beautiful and unique. Bubbles are also temporary and once they pop they become part of the universe, just as we do when we die. When people encounter bubbles it is a like a rare moment of magic. They symbolize our childhood innocence, reminding us of a time when life was simple and carefree. When we see these glass-like orbs dancing in the air they remind us to live in the moment, let go, dance with a stranger, be silly - have a bubblegasm!

mutant_vehicles.name: Bugaboo 2
mutant_vehicles.description: Bugaboo2 ( soon to be renamed) is a fun monster mutant vehicle that will make you smile and laugh

mutant_vehicles.name: Bulgarian Kuker
mutant_vehicles.description: Bulgarian KUKER, produced by HitterPetter Production House L.A., represents the 5000 year old Bulgarian tradition of KUKERI RITUAL DANCERS - masked people dressed up in animalistic outfits to scare away evil spirits and bring prosperity and happiness to the village.

mutant_vehicles.name: BumpBed
mutant_vehicles.description: Bumping double decker 2 story vibrant bright glowing mobile and sound mutant vehicle with DJ booth and dance floor, hand painted art, funky faux fur interior and thousands of LEDs .

mutant_vehicles.name: Bumpy
mutant_vehicles.description: Take a ride on Bumpy to relive the excitement and fun of your childhood carnival experiences.

mutant_vehicles.name: Burning Man Bunny Car
mutant_vehicles.description:
Take a break from the everyday and hop into the pink fur-lined world of The Bunny Car—Burning Man's heartwarming mutant vehicle.
More than just a vehicle, The Bunny Car lifts spirits, sparks laughter, and leaves a dusty trail of memories and wonder.

Get in. Hold on. And let The Bunny Car take you there.

mutant_vehicles.name: BURNSTREAM POINT LIGHTHOUSE
mutant_vehicles.description: Burnstream Point Lighthouse is a nomadic lighthouse, roaming the playa and welcoming travelers home! When you see the sweeping beam of the vintage rotating DCB-36 beacon you will know you have found your way to the exact place you should be. Standing over thirty feet tall and fully mobile, the lighthouse is one-of-a-kind! Come join us for a ride. We are looking forward to meeting you!

mutant_vehicles.name: Butterfly love aura
mutant_vehicles.description: From a cocoon of love comes this butterfly to warm the hearts of everyone around. Lighting the way for all of our burner friends. We invite you to take a smaller more detailed ride on something slightly more delicate! Built by a crew from Sacramento, this piece is one of a kind!

mutant_vehicles.name: Byrdhaüs
mutant_vehicles.description: Fly away with the majestic mountain blue bird across the desert, rest in its home or under the wings for some shade during the days, and enjoy its musical calls and vibrant lights through the night.

mutant_vehicles.name: CA$H Goblin
mutant_vehicles.description: The Ca$h Goblin is an assemblage poem to the crass capitalism of our culture and, be default, a growing number of people's approach to BM. The Ca$h Goblin gobbles everyone's cash and wants to know how much you spent on your MV, your art, and who paid for it.

mutant_vehicles.name: Caballo del Sol
mutant_vehicles.description: Life sized rideable horse made from repurposed horseshoes powered by electricity.

mutant_vehicles.name: Calypso
mutant_vehicles.description: Fire breathing steampunk pontoon ship

mutant_vehicles.name: Candyland Car
mutant_vehicles.description: All aboard the Candyland Car! We're on our way to Willy Wonka's factory to raid his stockpiles and create some mischief with the Umpa Lumpas!

mutant_vehicles.name: Cash Only
mutant_vehicles.description: A life size version of an operational closed circuit camera from the 1980s era capturing all the dusty Roving Voyeurism of BRC brought to you by BRCCTV. Only to be broadcast on the sides of the vehicle with an dLED matrix

mutant_vehicles.name: Cat of a Different Color (CDC)
mutant_vehicles.description: CDC (Cat of a Different Color) is an animatronic, lighted cat car.

mutant_vehicles.name: Chairman of the Bored
mutant_vehicles.description: The world's largest power chair

mutant_vehicles.name: Chatterbox
mutant_vehicles.description: Immerse yourself in the vibrant cacophony of creativity with the Chatterbox Art Car. This rolling masterpiece serves as a mobile platform for spontaneous conversations, fueled by the energy of the playa. Adorned with mesmerizing humans and pulsating with music, the Chatterbox invites participants to engage in dynamic dialogues, forging connections that transcend boundaries. Join the journey aboard this mobile marvel and experience the magic of community, expression, laughter and exploration!

mutant_vehicles.name: CHEESUS SAVES (formerly blue cheese)
mutant_vehicles.description: We are a magical block of cheese bringing outstanding grilled cheese, music and mediocre conversion to the furthest corners of the playa. Find us deep playa or at a dance party serving up our delicious body of crust (grilled cheese squares cooked to perfection) or an ice cold beverage from our cooler. When you see the cheese glowing in the distance stop by and see if we are serving...

mutant_vehicles.name: Chelonix Art Car
mutant_vehicles.description: Chelonix is a giant glowing space turtle roaming the playa. Built on a box truck platform, the vehicle features a wooden turtle shell structure, an animatronic head, inflatable flippers, and a central dance floor where participants can gather, climb, and explore. Flowing fabrics conceal the truck beneath and evoke an underwater kelp forest moving through the desert wind. By day, Chelonix appears as a playful ocean creature crossing the dust. By night, thousands of LEDs transform it into a luminous cosmic turtle swimming through Black Rock City.

mutant_vehicles.name: Chester
